note: One home for the beat map: video/review/build_review.py renders it on the review page and writes video/beat_map.md from it. Times are estimates until the TTS files exist. 'say' is the narrator unless a line starts with 'Coach:' (the coach's own, flatter voice). 'screen' describes everything visible. Words that appear on screen are in double quotes and stay at 5 or fewer per screen; eyebrows such as NO MEMORY · 13:28 are evidence labels and don't count. From draft 4, the beats with our system (6, 8, 9) are cut from the demo page's video of the stage-40 run: the footage on the left, the page's live panel on the right (world model's next-action predictions, the coach's latest answer, d1's next move and the checklist), so every shot shows what the models actually output at that second. From draft 6 the comparison is a typical chef (one that only watches and talks: our coach without the rest of the system) against our whole system; memory is one part of it.

beats.label: The hook
beats.say: Ever thought of having a coaching chef in your house, teaching you to cook? Or even designing your own?
beats.screen: The learner's head-camera view as a meal begins: ingredients come out of the fridge, then the onion goes onto the chopping board. Over the footage, centred white text: "Your own coaching chef?", with "coaching chef" in italic serif. Nothing else on screen.
beats.sound: The music starts with the cooking: Bushwick Tarantella (Kevin MacLeod, CC BY 4.0), under the narration.

beats.label: The catch
beats.say: But a typical chef, one that only watches and talks, bumps into problems. It told our learner to crack the eggs fourteen times. The eggs were already in the pan.
beats.screen: Hard cut to the eggs cooking in the pan, full screen. A small white coach card slides in top-left: eyebrow OTHER CHEF · 13:28, line "Crack the eggs." A big red counter beside it rolls from ×1 to "×14" while the line is spoken.
beats.sound: The music dips; a soft tick on each count.

beats.label: Chapter 1 · Other chefs
beats.say: A typical chef repeats itself. Coach: Crack the eggs. Crack the eggs. Crack the eggs.
beats.screen: On a pale green paper card, a red numbered square "1" and the title "Other chefs" for one second. Then three hard cuts: the onion on the chopping board, the phone, the oil spray. Each shot gets the same red card "Crack the eggs." and the counter steps "×1", "×2", "×3".

beats.label: It forgets
beats.say: It forgets what you did. Our learner cracked the eggs at five minutes. At nine, it asks again.
beats.screen: Close-up of the learner cracking eggs into a bowl. At the bottom, the egg step icon fills green with "5:13". Hard cut to 8:54: the bowl of whisked eggs sits by the stove while the learner fetches a plate; the red card returns, eyebrow OTHER CHEF · 8:54, "Crack the eggs."
beats.sound: Tick as the icon fills, pop for the card.

beats.label: It can't tell what's done
beats.say: And it can't tell what's finished. The eggs are on the plate, and it says: heat the pan and add the onions.
beats.screen: The learner scrapes the scrambled eggs onto a plate. The red card appears: eyebrow OTHER CHEF · 13:59, "Add the onions." The shot holds on the finished plate for a moment.

beats.label: The turn
beats.say: So we designed an entire system around the chef.
beats.screen: The whole frame becomes solid memory green. Centred white text: "We designed a system.", with "system" in italic serif. A slow push-in.
beats.sound: The music drops out for this beat.

beats.label: Chapter 2 · With our system
beats.say: Start wherever you like. Our learner gets the plate ready first, and the chef goes along: fine, do it in parallel. Then the onion: keep going.
beats.screen: A green numbered square "2" and the title "With our system" for one second. Then the demo page's video: the learner on the left, the page's panel on the right (world model, coach, d1). The learner turns from the sink to the cottage-cheese plate; at 0:39 the coach's answer reaches the panel and a green card lands top-left, eyebrow OUR SYSTEM · 0:39, "Plate first? Fine." The coach's reply lifts out of the panel and grows to the centre, its line "fine to do in parallel" marked in green, holds for 2 s, then drops back. Hard cut to the onion being chopped (1:54); card "Keep going.", eyebrow OUR SYSTEM · 1:45, while the panel still shows that answer. When the world model's "peel onion" turns out right, the picture freezes for a second so its tick stays 2 s.
beats.sound: The music returns; pop on each card.

beats.label: It keeps track
beats.say: It keeps track: every action it sees is written down against a recipe step, so it always knows what has started and what is left.
beats.screen: A row of seven round step icons appears along the bottom, all grey outlines. Four two-second shots follow (the plate, the onion, the pan, the eggs), and with each one its icon fills green and shows the moment it was first seen: 0:13, 1:50, 4:36, 5:13.
beats.sound: A light tick on each fill.

beats.label: Only when it's needed
beats.say: It only speaks up when something is needed. The eggs still aren't cracked, so it steers our learner back to them. Then Liquid AI's d1 decision model lines up the next moves. Open the carton. Take an egg. Crack it. Our learner does all three.
beats.screen: The demo page's video, footage left, model panel right. The learner is at the phone; at 4:53 the coach's answer reaches the panel and a green card lands top-left, eyebrow OUR SYSTEM · 4:53, "Back to the eggs." The coach's reply lifts out of the panel and grows to the centre, its line "back to cracking and whisking the eggs" marked in green, holds for 2.5 s, then drops back. Under the card, the step row (2, 3 and 7 on, as the memory has them). Hard cut to 5:10: d1's top three in the panel are open package, break egg and take egg; the learner opens the carton, takes an egg and cracks it, and each of d1's rows gets a green tick as its move happens, on the words "open", "take", "crack"; the picture freezes half a second on each tick. A small LIQUID AI d1 label sits by the panel's decision-model header. The world model's rows get a tick whenever its prediction comes true (break egg, put shell). Step 1 fills as the memory marks it, at 5:16.
beats.sound: Pop for the card, a whoosh as the reply lifts and drops, a soft tick on each green tick and on the fill.

beats.label: Another dish
beats.say: On a bacon and egg sandwich, it suggests shredding the cheese while the eggs cook, and reminds you to season the eggs before you build the sandwich.
beats.screen: The demo page's video of the Bacon & Egg run, footage left, model panel right. 6:45: the learner readies the baguette and cuts it (6:49) while the coach's 6:17 answer is on the panel; green card "Shred cheese meanwhile." (eyebrow OUR SYSTEM · 6:17) and the reply lifts to the centre, its line "shredding the cheddar cheese while the eggs and bacon continue cooking" marked. The world model's "cut bread" and d1's "cut bread (step 6)" get green ticks as the cutting happens. Hard cut to 7:01, the next answer arrives; card "Season the eggs first." Hard cut to 9:19: salt goes into the learner's hand; the world model says pour salt and d1 says take salt and sprinkle salt, and each gets a tick as it happens.
beats.sound: Pops for the cards, a whoosh for the reply, soft ticks on the green ticks.

beats.label: Chapter 3 · How it works
beats.say: Here's the whole system. Meta's V-JEPA 2 world model watches the video and answers: what is the learner about to do? Muse Glimmer, the coach, reads the memory and answers: what matters now? And Liquid AI's d1 turns that into one next move, every second.
beats.screen: A numbered square "3" and "How it works". On pale green paper, white cards appear one at a time, joined by dashed arrows: Video, V-JEPA 2, Memory, Muse Glimmer, Liquid AI d1, Next move. The card being named lights up green with its question underneath: "What's next?", "What matters?", "One move." The kitchen keeps playing in a small rounded square, bottom-right.
beats.sound: A soft tick as each card lands.

beats.label: One part, up close
beats.say: Here is one part of it, up close. Each action, take egg, cut onion, spray oil, is mapped back to its recipe step, with the moment it was first seen.
beats.screen: On paper, a timeline of small action chips runs across the top ("take egg", "cut onion", "spray oil"). As each is spoken, its chip lifts off and drops into the matching slot of the step row below, which then shows its first-seen time.

beats.label: The result
beats.say: After the eggs were whisked, the other chef asked to crack them five more times. Ours: once. It still misses what the camera can't see, and that's what we're working on next.
beats.screen: Two tinted panels side by side, pale red and pale green, under a small eyebrow ASKED TO CRACK EGGS AFTER 7:41. Big numbers count up: "5" in the "Other chef" panel, "1" in the "Our system" panel. They hold while the limit is said.

beats.label: The close
beats.say: Your own coaching chef, designed as a whole system.
beats.screen: The finished plate being seasoned, dimmed. White text: "Your own coaching chef.", with "coaching chef" in italic serif, echoing the opening. Then a paper card with the project name and the credits: built with Meta V-JEPA 2, Muse Glimmer and Liquid AI d1; footage HD-EPIC, University of Bristol, CC BY-NC 4.0; music "Bushwick Tarantella" by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0.
